# The real bottleneck: encoding and fonts
For **English** translations, the pain is **memory** — Japanese glyphs pack more meaning into the same bytes. For **Chinese** translations, the core problems are **encoding** and **font**:
  • Shift JIS, the encoding used by most PSP games, covers 6,355 kanji
  • GB2312, a subset of GB18030 (87,887 characters), has 6,763 characters
  • Only 3,331 share the same encoding in Unicode
Shift JIS6,355
GB23126,763
3,331shared in Unicode
The characters a translation needs simply aren't in the Japanese encoding.
arguments.note: English translations hit a memory wall: Japanese text conveys more meaning per byte. Chinese translations hit an encoding-and-font wall instead. Sources: roughly 600 Chinese fan translations vs 57 English ones on romhacking.net (count as of the recording); Shift JIS 6,355 kanji, GB2312 6,763 characters (a subset of GB18030's 87,887), and 3,331 characters shared at the same Unicode encoding — from the speaker's research notes.
